evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to published research (Chan et al., 2015).

claim: All human bNAbs against flaviviruses identified in the context of natural infection so far were isolated from plasmablasts of individuals sequentially exposed to at least two DENV serotypes.
source: To our knowledge, all human bNAbs against flaviviruses identified in the context of natural infection so far, including J9 and J8, were isolated from plasmablasts of individuals sequentially exposed to at least two DENV serotypes (Dejnirattisai et al., 2015; Xu et al., 2012; Zanini et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to published research (Dejnirattisai et al., 2015; Xu et al., 2012; Zanini et al., 2018).

claim: Sequential infection with heterologous DENV serotypes or HIV strains has been shown to broaden and strengthen the polyclonal neutralizing antibody response.
source: Sequential infection with heterologous DENV serotypes or HIV strains has been shown to broaden and strengthen the polyclonal neutralizing antibody response (Cortez et al., 2012; Patel et al., 2017; Tsai et al., 2015; Tsai et al., 2013).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to published research (Cortez et al., 2012; Patel et al., 2017; Tsai et al., 2015; Tsai et al., 2013).

claim: One proposed model is that low affinity, cross-reactive antibody secreting B-cell clones elicited by primary DENV exposure are reactivated during secondary infection to undergo further affinity maturation resulting in antibodies with more broad and potent neutralizing activity.
source: One proposed model is that low affinity, cross-reactive antibody secreting B-cell clones elicited by primary DENV exposure are reactivated during secondary infection to undergo further affinity maturation resulting in antibodies with more broad and potent neutralizing activity (Patel et al., 2017).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to published research (Patel et al., 2017).

claim: The relatively high level of somatic hypermutation already present in J9 and J8 at day four post-fever onset following secondary DENV infection suggests a recall response.
source: Although the relatively high level of somatic hypermutation already present in J9 and J8 at day four post-fever onset following secondary DENV infection suggests a recall response, repertoire analysis from earlier time points would be required to determine whether the memory B cell clones from which these bNAbs were derived underwent further mutation to achieve neutralization breadth and potency.
evidence: This is an inference based on the experimental results regarding somatic hypermutation levels.

claim: Despite the presence of plasmablast-derived bNAbs such as J9 and J8 during acute secondary infection, the donors from which these antibodies were isolated developed severe dengue disease.
source: Despite the presence of plasmablast-derived bNAbs such as J9 and J8, and those belonging to the EDE class during acute secondary infection, the donors from which these antibodies were isolated developed severe dengue disease (Dejnirattisai et al., 2015; Zanini et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to published research (Dejnirattisai et al., 2015; Zanini et al., 2018).

claim: J9 and J8 likely appeared too late to mitigate pathogenesis as they were derived from plasmablasts 4 days after onset of fever, and just one day prior to diagnosis of severe disease.
source: J9 and J8 likely appeared too late to mitigate pathogenesis as they were derived from plasmablasts 4 days after onset of fever, and just one day prior to diagnosis of severe disease (Table 1).
evidence: This is an inference based on the timing of plasmablast sampling and disease progression shown in Table 1.

claim: The rapid and massive plasmablast activation following acute DENV infection is coincident with the onset of severe symptoms and has been proposed to contribute to immunopathology.
source: The rapid and massive plasmablast activation following acute DENV infection is also coincident with the onset of severe symptoms and has been proposed to contribute to immunopathology (Wrammert et al., 2012).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to published research (Wrammert et al., 2012).

claim: J9/J8-like bNAbs make up a minor component of the overall polyclonal antibody response, as they minimally contribute to the neutralizing activity of patient 013 serum.
source: Our data also suggest that J9/J8-like bNAbs make up a minor component of the overall polyclonal antibody response, as they minimally contribute to the neutralizing activity of patient 013 serum (Figure 5—figure supplement 4).
evidence: This is an inference based on the experimental results shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 4.

claim: Though expanded, the J9/J8 clonal family is not the largest in patient 013, at least not in the acute phase sample tested.
source: Additionally, B cell receptor repertoire analysis revealed that though expanded, the J9/J8 clonal family is not the largest in this donor (Table 3), at least not in the acute phase sample tested.
evidence: This is a description of the experimental results shown in Table 3.

claim: Immunogen design to elicit bNAbs may require masking of immunodominant epitopes targeted by weakly neutralizing antibodies to focus the antibody response on the desired epitope.
source: Although based on the analysis of a single donor, one implication of our finding is that immunogen design to elicit bNAbs may require masking of immunodominant epitopes targeted by weakly neutralizing antibodies to focus the antibody response on the desired epitope (Weidenbacher and Kim, 2019).
evidence: This is a speculative statement about vaccine design implications supported by a citation to published research (Weidenbacher and Kim, 2019).
